Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

Record the acquisition type, duration, budget and closure cap, launch gate, stop and pause rules, and which measures required complete outcome windows.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Historical design card — approved 2026 Helio Start paid-search pilot", "folder": "historical-design-cards", "body": "Historical design card

Pilot: Helio Start paid-search pilot
Decision vintage: 2026
Status: Closed after the admission cap was reached; this card records the approved design and its governing evidence boundaries, not a later recommendation.

Acquisition type
- High-intent paid search.
- One bounded paid-acquisition pilot; no automatic expansion, second batch, pipeline target, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.
- Existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, assisted-routing, and suppression rules remained unchanged. Paid source was not permitted to bypass those rules.

Duration
- Maximum: six weeks.
- Scheduled launch: April 15, 2026.
- Time boundary: May 26, 2026.
- The pilot closed earlier, on May 18, when the 50-admitted-workspace cap was reached.

Budget and closure cap
- Maximum budget: $15,000 in spend.
- Hard closure at the earlier of:
  - $15,000 in spend; or
  - 50 admitted workspaces.
- Actual cap close: 50 admitted workspaces at $14,420 in spend, before the spend cap and May 26 time limit. Paid traffic was turned off and the admitted cohort was fixed; no additional admission could enter the pilot.
- The paired limits were exposure caps, not an expected acquisition cost, observed cost per admission, or cost-per-admission ceiling.

Launch gate
Paid traffic could not begin on budget approval alone. The gate required:
- Budget approval for the six-week high-intent paid-search shape.
- A complete nonproduction paid-source attribution preflight across 24 cases: 8 expected admissions, 8 expected assisted routes, and 8 expected fail-closed or suppressed outcomes.
- Every case reconciled from eligibility-flow start through its final route, including admission and assisted routing.
- No case bypassed an existing lifecycle branch, hold, or suppression.
- Assisted-route reasons and account-level support minutes were recordable from first contact.
- Daniela’s production/preflight sign-off after defects were corrected and the full 24-case set was rerun.

Historical gate record
- April 2: budget approved; launch authorization was explicitly still pending preflight.
- April 8: preflight failed at 23/24 because one assisted-route case reached Customer Success with a blank paid-source value; paid traffic remained blocked.
- April 11: the corrected full 24-case reconciliation passed; lifecycle behavior remained unchanged and the pilot was scheduled, not yet live.
- April 15: paid traffic opened after the cleared gate.

Stop rules
- Immediate stop if any unsupported applicant entered the admitted path.
- Stop/close at the first applicable exposure limit: $15,000 spend, 50 admitted workspaces, or the six-week time boundary.
- Paid traffic remained off after closure; the fixed cohort continued into its predeclared outcome windows.

Pause rules
- Pause if a routing or instrumentation failure prevented paid-source reconciliation from eligibility-flow start through the final route.
- After at least 20 admissions, pause if more than 10% of admitted workspaces exceeded 90 account-level support minutes.
- A pause required bounded/corrected records, rerun reconciliation where applicable, and authorized restart; it did not authorize a bypass of existing lifecycle behavior.

Measures and evidence windows
Leading operating measure:
- Day-7 first integration could be reported only as a leading operating indicator. It was not mature acquisition, scale, revenue, pipeline, or forecast evidence.

Measures requiring complete outcome windows before any mature claim:
- Paid-active status.
- Refund-adjusted collected cash.
- Account-level support effort, including the support burden and high-effort tail.

The mature measures required complete day-90 windows for the fixed admitted cohort. A complete outcome packet did not automatically authorize another paid batch and did not support causal acquisition, incrementality, scalable-channel, pipeline, or forecast claims. Paid-source reconciliation, unsupported-admission checks, and support-load monitoring remained operating controls separate from the mature outcome claims."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_132_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The card records the approved six-week high-intent paid-search pilot with a maximum $15,000 budget and closure at the earlier of $15,000 spent or 50 admissions. Budget approval was not launch approval; paid traffic remained blocked until attribution could reconcile through admission and assisted routing. The pilot stops if an unsupported applicant is admitted, pauses if routing or instrumentation prevents reconciliation, and after 20 admissions pauses if more than 10% exceed 90 support minutes.
